        "contents": "extension Color {\n    init(hex: String) {\n        let hex = hex.trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet.alphanumerics.inverted)\n        var int: UInt64 = 0\n        Scanner(string: hex).scanHexInt64(&amp;int)\n        let a, r, g, b: UInt64\n        switch hex.count {\n        case 6:\n            (a, r, g, b) = (255, (int &gt;&gt; 16) &amp; 0xFF, (int &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF, int &amp; 0xFF)\n        case 8:\n            (a, r, g, b) = ((int &gt;&gt; 24) &amp; 0xFF, (int &gt;&gt; 16) &amp; 0xFF, (int &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF, (int &gt;&gt; 0) &amp; 0xFF)\n        default:\n            (a, r, g, b) = (255, 200, 200, 200)\n        }\n        self.init(\n            .sRGB,\n            red: Double(r) / 255,\n            green: Double(g) / 255,\n            blue: Double(b) / 255,\n            opacity: Double(a) / 255\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// extension KnownDevice: Identifiable {\n//     public var id: String { DeviceID }\n// }\n\n#Preview {\n    @Previewable @State var device = KnownDevice(name: \"Test Device\", deviceID: \"12345\", color: .blue)\n    DeviceRowView(device: device, cache: DeviceLocationCacheStore.shared)\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * ColorExtensions.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2025-01-25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n// MARK: - Color Extension for Contrast Adjustment\nextension Color {\n    /// Adjusts device color for better contrast in light/dark mode\n    /// - Parameters:\n    ///   - deviceColor: The original device color\n    ///   - colorScheme: Current color scheme (light/dark)\n    /// - Returns: Adjusted color with better contrast\n    static func adjustedDeviceColor(_ deviceColor: Color, for colorScheme: ColorScheme) -&gt; Color {\n        // Convert to UIColor for easier manipulation\n        let uiColor = UIColor(deviceColor)\n        \n        // Get RGB components\n        var red: CGFloat = 0\n        var green: CGFloat = 0\n        var blue: CGFloat = 0\n        var alpha: CGFloat = 0\n        \n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;red, green: &amp;green, blue: &amp;blue, alpha: &amp;alpha)\n        \n        // Calculate luminance to determine if color is dark or light\n        let luminance = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue\n        \n        switch colorScheme {\n        case .light:\n            // In light mode, if the color is too light (white-ish), make it lighter gray\n            if luminance &gt; 0.85 {\n                // Make it a light gray instead of white\n                return Color(red: 0.8, green: 0.8, blue: 0.8)\n            }\n        case .dark:\n            // In dark mode, if the color is too dark (black-ish), make it darker gray\n            if luminance &lt; 0.15 {\n                // Make it a dark gray instead of black\n                return Color(red: 0.3, green: 0.3, blue: 0.3)\n            }\n        @unknown default:\n            break\n        }\n        \n        // Return original color if no adjustment needed\n        return deviceColor\n    }\n}",

        },
        "contents": "    static func buildPayload(devices: [KnownDevice], locations: [CachedDeviceLocation], ownDeviceID: String) -&gt; WidgetSharedPayload {\n        var entries: [WidgetDeviceData] = []\n        var ownDevice: WidgetDeviceData?\n\n        for device in devices {\n            guard let location = locations.first(where: { $0.deviceID == device.DeviceID }) else { continue }\n            guard let entry = WidgetDeviceDataBuilder.makeEntry(device: device, location: location) else { continue }\n            entries.append(entry)\n            if device.DeviceID == ownDeviceID {\n                ownDevice = entry\n            }\n        }\n\n        return WidgetSharedPayload(\n            devices: entries,\n            ownDeviceID: ownDeviceID,\n            ownDevice: ownDevice\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - Helpers\n\nprivate enum WidgetDeviceDataBuilder {\n    static func makeEntry(device: KnownDevice, location: CachedDeviceLocation) -&gt; WidgetDeviceData? {\n        WidgetDeviceData(\n            id: device.DeviceID,\n            name: device.DeviceName,\n            latitude: location.latitude,\n            longitude: location.longitude,\n            locality: location.locality,\n            country: location.country,\n            timestamp: location.timestamp,\n            accuracy: location.accuracy,\n            color: WidgetColorFactory.color(from: device.DeviceColor)\n        )\n    }\n}\n\nprivate enum WidgetColorFactory {\n    static func color(from uiColor: UIColor?) -&gt; WidgetColor? {\n        guard let uiColor else { return nil }\n        var r: CGFloat = 0\n        var g: CGFloat = 0\n        var b: CGFloat = 0\n        var a: CGFloat = 0\n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;r, green: &amp;g, blue: &amp;b, alpha: &amp;a)\n        return WidgetColor(red: Double(r), green: Double(g), blue: Double(b), alpha: Double(a))\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "    /// Spacing between multiple arrows on the same edge or at corners.\n    private let arrowSpacing: CGFloat = 80\n\n    /// Segment length (in points) used to visualize distance.\n    private let segmentLength: CGFloat = 3\n    /// Spacing (in points) between arrow segments for clear separation.\n    private let segmentSpacing: CGFloat = 1\n    /// Maximum number of distance segments to display.\n    private let maxArrowSegments: Int = 10\n    /// Number of arrow segments representing the distance.\n    /// Shows 1 segment per 50 km (capped by &#96;maxArrowSegments&#96;).\n    private var arrowSegments: Int {\n        let segments = Int(distanceInKM / 50.0)\n        return min(segments, maxArrowSegments)\n    }\n\n    // Computed property to determine the best text color for contrast\n    private var textColor: Color {\n        // Convert device color to UIColor to check brightness\n        let uiColor = UIColor(deviceColor)\n        var red: CGFloat = 0\n        var green: CGFloat = 0\n        var blue: CGFloat = 0\n        var alpha: CGFloat = 0\n        \n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;red, green: &amp;green, blue: &amp;blue, alpha: &amp;alpha)\n        \n        // Calculate perceived brightness using standard formula\n        let brightness = (0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue)\n        \n        // Use white text for dark backgrounds, black text for light backgrounds\n        return brightness &gt; 0.5 ? .black : .white\n    }\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        // Renders the arrow when the device is outside the visible bounds.",

NSColor analog\n#endif\n    }\n}\n\n// Zusatz-Utilities für Cache-Key und Bild-Cache\nextension Color {\n    /// Stabile RGBA-Repräsentation für Cache-Keys\n    func rgbaKey() -&gt; String {\n#if canImport(UIKit)\n        let uiColor = UIColor(self)\n        var r: CGFloat = 0, g: CGFloat = 0, b: CGFloat = 0, a: CGFloat = 0\n        uiColor.getRed(&amp;r, green: &amp;g, blue: &amp;b, alpha: &amp;a)\n        return String(format: \"r%.3fg%.3fb%.3fa%.3f\", r, g, b, a)\n#elseif canImport(AppKit)\n        return String(describing: self)\n#else\n        return String(describing: self)\n#endif\n    }\n}\n\nfinal class MiataruMapMarkerImageCache {\n    static let shared = MiataruMapMarkerImageCache()\n    private let cache = NSCache&lt;NSString, PlatformImage&gt;()\n    private init() {\n        cache.countLimit = 256\n    }\n    func image(for key: String) -&gt; PlatformImage? {\n        cache.object(forKey: key as NSString)\n    }\n    func set(_ image: PlatformImage, for key: String, cost: Int = 0) {\n        cache.setObject(image, forKey: key as NSString, cost: cost)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct MiataruMapMarker: View {\n    @Environment(\\.colorScheme) private var colorScheme",

String ?? \"\"\n        if let deviceIDsArray = aDecoder.decodeObject(forKey: \"deviceIDs\") as? Updated the default device color to randomly select a vivid color instead of gray.

1. **Added a helper function** `randomVividColor()` that selects from: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink
2. **Updated the initial state** of `deviceColor` to use this function instead of `.gray`

New devices now get a random vivid color by default. Users can still change it via the color picker. The function defaults to blue if selection fails (unlikely).

No linter errors. Ready to use.
